title.narrative: Lifesaving response to displacement and famine

description.narrative: ltpgtAfter more than a year of the war, an estimated 10.7 million people (2.1 million families) are now internally displaced in Sudan.nbspnbspAbout 25.6 million people – over half of the population of Sudan – face Crisis or worse levels of food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above) between June and September 2024, coinciding with the lean season, according to the latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Acute Food Insecurity Snapshot.nbspltbrgtOf these, 8.5 million are experiencing emergency levels of hunger and about 755,000 people on the brink of famine – during the same period in ten states, including Greater Darfur (all five states), South and North Kordofan, Blue Nile, Al Jazirah, and Khartoum.lt/pgtltpgtThe project will address food security needs of the displaced and host communities by providing 3 months of MEB to the 1664 households in Thobo and Western Kadugli. According to the latest FSMU report(April 2024) 34% of the households in Thobo and 47% of the households in Western Kadugli are internally displaced. This means that the communities are experiencing increased pressure on basic services and food provision for the newly displaced. DCA field visits to the affected areas have shown IDP-s eating wild fruits, leaves and roots to survive the lean season. Quality of diet is poor in both host-and IDP households according to FSMU report eg. in Western Kadugli 67% of host communities and 59% of IDP communities experience poor diet.nbsplt/pgtltpgtResponse:lt/pgtltpgtMPCAlt/pgtltpgtDCA proposes to utilize MPCA to support 1,200 households with 3 rounds of current Sudan MEB (180,000 SDG-s) in Thobo and Western Kadugli which will be distributed through an e-voucher modality. The programme will include working closely with local traders who provide the goods and commodities to the beneficiaries using the e-voucher cards. The modality avoids direct cash exchange thereby providing a safer and more accessible way for beneficiaries to receive their items. Market volunteers will be recruited for 4-5 months to support the setup of the programme, to do market monitoring, registration of beneficiaries, distribution and redemption of the MEB-s. Percentage of the cash amount will be provided as cash back option for beneficiaries to purchase items from smaller traders eg. vegetables and meat. The programme will include MEAL support activities including complaints-and feedback mechanism, baseline-and verification survey, Bi-weekly market-and price monitoring, post distribution monitoring survey. ltbrgtThe whole cash programme is done in coordination with other actors(SP, NRC and IRC) who work in cash interventions in the project areas. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtConflict sensitivity:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtDue to increasing tensions between IDP and host communities stemming from a due to lack of available resources DCA proposes to include activities on conflict sensitivity. Partners will be conducting trainings and awareness sessions among communities and leaders on social cohesion and importance of peaceful co-existence. The teams will focus on the community leaders and selection committee members who are trained in humanitarian principles, conflict resolution, importance on vulnerable population and assistance. lt/pgt
